q: In Philippine construction vernacular, a tinsmith is called:
ref: Common Philippine construction vernacular; no single authoritative standard, and usage may vary by region and practitioner. Figure: Know-How Architecture InstaFlashCards.
n: “Latero” = tinsmith. Origin: Spanish latero “tinsmith”, from lata “tin plate, tin can”.

q: In Philippine construction vernacular, carpentry is called:
ref: Common Philippine construction vernacular; no single authoritative standard, and usage may vary by region and practitioner.
n: “Karpinteria” = carpentry. Origin: Spanish carpintería, from carpintero “carpenter”.

q: What is the vernacular term for Foreman?
ref: Common Philippine construction vernacular; no single authoritative standard, and usage may vary by region and practitioner. Figure: Know-How Architecture InstaFlashCards.
n: “Kapatas / Maestro de Obra” = foreman. Origin: kapatas is Spanish capataz “foreman”; maestro de obra is “master of the works”.

q: In Philippine construction vernacular, a contractor is called:
ref: Common Philippine construction vernacular; no single authoritative standard, and usage may vary by region and practitioner. Figure: Know-How Architecture InstaFlashCards.
n: “Kontratista” = contractor. Origin: Spanish contratista, from contrato. Same root as English “contract”.

q: In Philippine construction vernacular, a laborer is called:
ref: Common Philippine construction vernacular; no single authoritative standard, and usage may vary by region and practitioner.
n: “Piyon” = laborer. Origin: Spanish peón “day laborer, foot soldier”, the root of English “pawn”.

q: What is the vernacular term for Architect?
ref: Common Philippine construction vernacular; no single authoritative standard, and usage may vary by region and practitioner.
n: “Architekto” = architect. Origin: Spanish arquitecto, from Greek arkhitekton “chief builder”.

q: What is the vernacular term for Electrician?
ref: Common Philippine construction vernacular; no single authoritative standard, and usage may vary by region and practitioner.
n: “Electrisista” = electrician. Origin: Spanish electricista, from electricidad.

q: What is the vernacular term for Plumber?
ref: Common Philippine construction vernacular; no single authoritative standard, and usage may vary by region and practitioner.
n: “Tubero” = plumber. Origin: Spanish tubero, from tubo “pipe”. Someone who works with tubes.

q: In Philippine construction vernacular, a mason is called:
ref: Common Philippine construction vernacular; no single authoritative standard, and usage may vary by region and practitioner. Figure: Know-How Architecture InstaFlashCards.
n: “Kantero” = mason. Origin: Spanish cantero “stonemason”, from canto “stone, edge”.
